sentences.text: [B.A. Nos.664 & 647 of 2023] Dated this the 20th day of April, 2023
The petitioner in these bail applications is the 2 nd accused in Crime No.33 of 2023 and 32 of 2023 of Chavakkad police station.
Bail Application No.647 of 2023 was filed in respect of Crime No.33 of 2023, where as Bail Application No.664 of 2023 was filed in respect of Crime No.32 of 2023.

The offences alleged in both the aforesaid crimes are under Sections 406, 420 read with Section 34 of the I.P.C.
2.

The common case of the prosecution is as follows;
The petitioner/2nd accused is the staff of Chavakkad branch of a financial institution by name 'Safe and Strong Business Consultants', in which the 1st accused is the Managing Director.
The said institution had collected huge amounts from the B.A. Nos.664 & 647 of 2023 general public as deposit, offering high returns.
However, later they did not provide interest as offered and the amount was also not refunded.
The respective complaints were submitted in such circumstances and accordingly the aforesaid crimes were registered.
These applications for anticipatory bail were submitted by the petitioner in such circumstance, as she apprehends arrest.

3. Heard Sri. Sumodh Madhavan Nair, learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner in both the cases and Sri. C.N. Prabhakaran, learned Public Prosecutor appearing in Bail Application No.647 of 2023 and Sri. M.P. Prasanth in Bail Application No.664 of 2023.
4.
The learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is only an employee of the said establishment and she was not having any control over the affairs of the company.
The main transactions were being conducted by the 1 st accused/Managing Director.

According to the B.A.
Nos.664 & 647 of 2023 petitioner, she was not at all aware of the criminal intention of the 1st accused and she performed her duty as per her terms of employment as directed by the 1st accused.

It is further pointed out that the petitioner is prepared to abide by any condition imposed by this Aswani V.V vs State Of Kerala on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71595747/
2 Court and shall co-operate with the investigation.
5.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application, pointing out that the 1 st accused is already arrested in connection with the case and is under detention.
Hundreds of cases are registered against the 1st accused in various police station across the State.
It is also pointed out that, the petitioner being a staff of the establishment, cannot wriggle out from the responsibilities.
The matter is under investigation and if the petitioner is released on bail, it is likely to hamper the process of investigation.
6. I have gone through the records and heard the B.A. Nos.664 & 647 of 2023 contentions raised by the learned Counsel on both sides.
It is true that there are some allegations against the petitioner.

However, it is an undisputed fact that the petitioner is only a staff of the establishment in question,
and the main culprit is already arrested and is under detention.
The petitioner is a lady and there is no criminal antecedents for her.

7. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case and also taking into account the fact that the 1st accused is already arrested, I am of the view that the custodial interrogation of the petitioner may not necessary.
It would be sufficient if the co- operation of the petitioner with the investigation is ensured.
iv) The petitioner shall appear before the investigating officer between 10.00 a.m and 11.00 a.m on every Wednesday until filing of the final report.
v) The petitioner shall also appear before the investigating officer as and when required by him.

B.A. Nos.664 & 647 of 2023 vi) The petitioner shall not commit any offence of like nature while on bail.

3 vii) The petitioner shall not make any attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses, directly or through any other person, or any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
viii) The petitioner shall not leave State of Kerala without the permission of the trial Court.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In such circumstances, these applications are disposed of with the following directions:
i) The petitioner shall surrender before the Investigation officer for the purpose of ensuring his B.A. Nos.664 & 647 of 2023 co-operation, within a period of two weeks from the date of the order, for subjecting herself for interrogation;
ii) After interrogation, the petitioner shall be released on bail, on the very same day of surrender upon the petitioner executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/- with two solvent sureties each for the like sum, to the satisfaction of the investigating officer;
iii) The petitioner shall fully co-operate with the investigation, including subjecting herself to the deemed police custody for the purpose of recovery, if any, as and when demanded.
iv) The petitioner shall appear before the investigating officer between 10.00 a.m and 11.00 a.m on every Wednesday until filing of the final report.
v) The petitioner shall also appear before the investigating officer as and when required by him.
